chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated to us, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from the one he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And their prayer was, at the House, not but warbling and applause.» He said: Whistling and handclapping.

key_terms.والتَّصْفِيقُ: And the act of clapping hands

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic term 'maka' wa tasdiya' mean in the context of pre-Islamic prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the Quranic terms 'maka' and 'tasdiya' specifically denote whistling and handclapping, highlighting the superficiality of the Quraysh's pre-Islamic prayer which lacked contemplation. This exegetical detail underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the spiritual depth and presence of heart in worship, contrasting ritualistic noise with true devotion. The interpretation aligns with classical tafsir traditions that view these sounds as markers of the Jahiliyyah era's distinct liturgical practices.
